articles.title: The UAE embraces AI for kindergartners
articles.summary:
In September, Henry Price observed a classroom of 7- to 8-year-olds learn about the Stone Age. They discussed and wrote about cave paintings, then put on virtual reality headsets to explore them.
The founding principal of Rugby School Dubai hopes his students will soon study ancient Egypt the same way — reading about it, creating artwork, and then stepping inside a virtual pyramid, or using artificial intelligence to “interview” a pharaoh.
“AI does not replace reading, writing, discussion, or creativity. It enhances them and opens new doors,” Price told Rest of World. “We want our students to be excited by AI, but never [be] passive users. We want children who use AI to ask better questions, not children who rely on it to give them all the answers.”
The United Arab Emirates recently became the first country to make AI a required K-12 subject.
That puts the country on one side of a growing global debate over what children should learn about AI and when they should encounter it. While the UAE and China are treating early AI literacy as a national priority, some Western governments are moving in the opposite direction. New York City introduced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI in public schools from preschool through grade eight, citing concerns about children’s mental health. Norway has also enacted a similar near-ban for primary school children.

articles.title: Google Play now lets anyone build private, vibe-coded apps that run on Android | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Your vibe-coded applications can now be easily run on Android smartphones without having to first go public on the Google Play Store, the tech giant announced on Tuesday. A new feature will allow users to launch their own personal apps on their device via Google Play using their standard Google account, but they will remain completely private.
These personal apps won’t show up in Google Play’s search or listing pages, and won’t be shared with anyone except for the app’s creator.
The idea comes as more people are experimenting with building their own applications via AI for specific, personal needs. However, being able to use that app on their own Android device has meant publishing to Google Play, making it accessible to the Play Store’s some 3 billion users. That led many to limit their vibe-coding efforts to web apps that could run on any device instead of something built natively for Android.
Now, Google says Android device owners can vibe-code an app using Google AI Studio, then launch it for their own use.
These apps are still required to comply with Google Play’s existing policies but allow users to experiment more directly with building apps for Android.
Initially, the feature will be available to users in the U.S., age 18 and up.
“That’s why the future of apps on Google Play is personal, secure, and built by everyone — and it’s why Play is leading the charge and moving from ‘there’s an app for that’ to ‘there’s an app for me,’” said Sam Bright, Google’s VP and GM for …

articles.title: Introducing Firefox Enterprise | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Mozilla introduces Firefox Enterprise
Institutions are recalculating who controls the technology they rely on. Mozilla has an independent option to offer.
For years, organizations consolidated technology around a small number of providers to make things simpler. Fewer systems. Tighter integrations. More economies of scale. But that consolidation went well beyond technology. It consolidated dependency, too. The resulting risks have been debated, studied, and challenged along the way, but concentration continued. More work, data and critical infrastructure kept moving to the same few providers, while credible alternatives narrowed.
The deeper that dependency runs, the harder and more costly it becomes to change course. When something fails, changes or falls outside an institution’s control, that dependency becomes a risk for CIOs and CISOs to manage.
Nowhere are these stakes more visible than in Europe. Now institutions are re-assessing. Governments are pushing for greater digital autonomy, while regulated industries face growing pressure to find and manage their dependencies.
There’s a name for much of this debate about technological control: “sovereignty.”
What digital sovereignty means in practice varies. Across Europe, governments are investing in the security and resilience of critical IT infrastructure, reducing strategic dependencies and putting technological autonomy higher on national agendas. Different approaches, same underlying concern. Strip away the regional polic…

articles.title: Microsoft is shutting its Nairobi engineering centre
articles.summary:
Microsoft is winding down its Africa Development Centre (ADC) in Nairobi, putting nearly 400 jobs at risk and reversing a seven-year effort to make Kenya a hub for building technology for global markets.
Two employees, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, told TechCabal that staff at the centre, housed in Dunhill Towers in Nairobi’s Westlands district, were called to a meeting on Monday morning and asked to meet with their managers by Friday, October 16, to discuss exit options, including severance terms.
The closure comes seven years after the company pledged more than $100 million to develop African tech talent, to make Nairobi one of its engineering hubs outside the US. It would unwind a project built on the promise that African engineers could build products for global markets without leaving the continent, raising questions about Microsoft’s long-term plans for engineering in Africa.
“We are communicating directly with employees in Kenya about proposed changes to our engineering operations,” a Microsoft spokesperson told TechCabal on Monday. “We recognise the uncertainty this brings and are keeping those discussions private. Microsoft remains committed to Kenya and will continue to have employees in the country while supporting the country’s ongoing digital transformation and innovation ambitions.”
The statement did not confirm the centre’s closure or specify how many employees would remain or when the changes would take effect.

articles.title: Les jaquettes iconiques de GTA sont nées à cause du 11 septembre
articles.summary:
Aucune jaquette n’a un style plus iconique que celles des jeux GTA, composées d’un assemblage de petits carrés très graphiques. Ce style est né avec GTA 3, presque par accident. Dan Houser, cofondateur et ancien vice-président de Rockstar Games, en a raconté la genèse dans un long entretien paru ce mardi 13 octobre sur IGN.
À l’origine, GTA 3 ne devait pas avoir la jaquette que tout le monde connaît aujourd’hui, devenue depuis la signature visuelle de la saga. En réalité, Rockstar Games a dû la changer à la dernière minute en raison des attentats du 11 septembre 2001, qui ont eu lieu un peu plus d’un mois avant la sortie du jeu, le 22 octobre.
La jaquette de GTA est devenue iconique à cause du 11 septembre
Le style en mosaïque introduit par GTA 3 est donc une conséquence du 11 septembre. Dan Houser raconte : « Ce qui est marrant, c’est que la pochette qui est devenue la pochette emblématique de GTA, Stephen Bliss l’a faite en environ deux soirées parce que l’ancienne pochette était probablement jugée trop choquante pour être publiée après le 11 septembre, car on y voyait des bâtiments en feu. »
L’illustrateur Stephen Bliss a lui-même confirmé cette version. Selon lui, la jaquette d’origine avait demandé environ six mois de travail et partait déjà à l’impression pour les fêtes quand les attentats ont frappé New York.
Sans le 11 septembre, GTA 3 aurait donc conservé son design d’origine et, a priori, n’aurait pas amorcé le style en mosaïque conservé par tous les épisodes qui on…

Le projet de loi de finances pour 2027, présenté le jeudi 1er octobre en Conseil des ministres, contient une ligne budgétaire inédite, alors même que l’État fait la chasse aux nouvelles dépenses pour tenter d’enrayer la dette. Intitulée « Soutien financier au nouveau nucléaire français » (programme 387), cette enveloppe de 137,8 millions d’euros a un rôle bien précis, et elle ne finance pas directement le chantier des six EPR2.
En réalité, cette enveloppe comble l’écart entre un taux d’intérêt soutenable pour EDF et le taux dont a besoin la Caisse des Dépôts, dont le Fonds d’épargne gère une partie de l’argent placé sur les Livrets A, LDDS et LEP.

Jusqu’à 330€ d’avantages avec nos offres Hello Prime ou Hello Prime Duo, dont 80€ cash à l’ouverture de compte !
Pour mesurer l’ampleur du montage, le Fonds d’épargne pourra prêter jusqu’à 60 milliards d’euros à la société de projet d’EDF, soit 60 % du devis de construction des six réacteurs, chiffré à 72,8 milliards d’euros (en euros de 2020). articles.title: The MFA Gaps Attackers are Still Exploiting
articles.summary:
On August 4, 2026, an Akira ransomware affiliate began spraying passwords against a SonicWall SSL VPN. Around seven minutes later, one attempt succeeded. The credentials were valid, and the VPN account had no multi-factor authentication (MFA) protecting it. Roughly two hours later, the attacker used RDP to access the domain controller and began enumerating Active Directory.
The ransomware deployment ultimately failed, but by then the attacker had already stolen credentials and file-share data.
It highlights an issue that is still common in 2026, where an organization might require MFA for Microsoft 365 and other SaaS applications while leaving certain access paths protected only by passwords. It’s this gap that attackers are regularly exploiting.
Stolen Credentials Remain a Valuable Tool for Attackers
Once an attacker has a valid account, they can begin interacting with the environment through the same authentication mechanisms used by legitimate employees and administrators. AI is adding another dimension to this problem by helping attackers operate at greater speed and scale.
The underlying identity tactics are largely unchanged: attackers still compromise identities, reuse credentials, escalate privileges and misuse legitimate access. The threat is that AI makes familiar techniques cheaper and easier to run at scale.

articles.title: Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a sparsely-activated architecture that scales large language model (LLM) capacity while keeping per-token compute low. Because its operations account for a large share of total compute time, inefficiencies there directly raise request latency and cost. Therefore, optimizing MoE operations through kernel engineering offers the largest opportunity for performance gains.
Fused MoE is a key optimization technique for the MoE architecture. A fused MoE system merges token routing, data shuffling, and specialized network calculations into a single batched operation on the GPU. This replaces executing those routing and expert computations as separate, sequential loop operations. While this provides latency advantages, it also brings complexity in kernel implementations and debugging capability. High GPU utilization for this architecture requires hardware-specific optimizations.
In this post, we describe the different kernel optimizations we implemented for fused MoE models and show you how you can benefit from this work. We used a representative MoE model as our primary example.

articles.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
articles.summary:
Microsoft today issued updates to fix more than 1,400 security vulnerabilities in its Windows operating systems and other software. Today’s epic patch batch dwarfs September’s record of nearly 1,000 fixes, which was already about ten times the normal monthly patch load from Redmond.
Just one of the weaknesses patched this week is considered a “zero day,” or already exploited in the wild. CVE-2026-96951 is a security feature bypass in the Windows Shell that affects Windows 10 and 11 systems, as well as some Server versions.
Windows 10 users might be wondering if they can still expect security updates after this month. Microsoft had been slated to stop shipping updates for Windows 10 systems in October 2025, but ended up adding another year of free updates after considerable pushback. A few months ago, Microsoft quietly extended that support for another year (until October 2027).
At least 78 of the flaws fixed this month are rated “critical,” meaning they could be exploited with little or no action by the user, and most of those critical bugs allow an attacker to execute code of their choice on the vulnerable system.
While Microsoft said there are no signs anyone is exploiting it yet, a security feature bypass in the .NET Framework (CVE-2026-108398) was publicly disclosed prior to today, potentially giving attackers advance time to work out how to exploit the bug.

articles.title: MIT startup says it can turn diesel trucks into cheaper hydrogen haulers — see it at Disrupt | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Diesel fuel powers everything from shipping to agriculture, and with prices hitting record highs in recent weeks, governments around the world are scrambling to contain the fallout.
For now, that’s meant releasing fuel from stockpiles, but in the coming years, the answer might be a new technology from an MIT startup called LNK Energies.
LNK has created a way to convert existing heavy-duty trucks from diesel to hydrogen, slashing pollution and costs while shielding operators from the price spikes that result from geopolitical instability like the war in Iran. “If you look at total cost of ownership of a Class 8 truck, it’s 13% cheaper than diesel,” Alexis Huynh, chief technology officer at LNK Energies, told TechCrunch. (Class 8 is the heaviest category of trucks, including big rigs.)
Automotive companies have been exploring the use of hydrogen in long-haul trucking in part because refilling a hydrogen tank is faster than recharging the massive batteries those trucks require. But hydrogen is challenging to move to refilling stations, and the pressure tanks required to store it on the truck are large and costly.
LNK’s approach is to carry hydrogen chemically attached to another compound. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers, or LOHCs, are liquids that can absorb and later release hydrogen, and they have been widely studied, but mostly for moving large quantities of hydrogen from refineries to fueling stations. Kaya es, según el escrito, su única heredera.
Tiene la custodia, ¿para qué quiere una tutela?
Son dos cosas distintas. Por un lado, la custodia decide dónde vive la niña y quién la cuida. Lo que es la tutela del patrimonio decide quién firma por ella cuando hay dinero de por medio, porque, como es normal, una menor no puede administrarlos.
En el primer caso, Klitschko decide el colegio; para firmar en su nombre un papel del banco, necesita otro tipo de autorización.
Por eso mismo, Klitschko pide ser tutor temporal, no definitivo, y el escrito define la medida como “urgent and essential”. Lo que dice buscar es proteger lo que hereda Kaya hasta que el tribunal designe a alguien que administre el patrimonio de la actriz, y según la petición, también quiere estar legitimado para impulsar ese nombramiento.

articles.title: Meta Says Hackers Took Code, Personal Data of 1,500 in GitHub Breach
articles.summary:
Meta is notifying roughly 1,500 people, most of them employees in the US, that their personal information was impacted after hackers got into some of the company’s GitHub repositories.
The intrusion was detected a few weeks ago. According to the tech giant, an outside group gained access to the repositories using an employee’s stolen credentials.
Meta’s security team shut down the attackers’ access and brought in GitHub and law enforcement. Notifications to the impacted individuals started going out on Tuesday.
Meta told SecurityWeek that 99% of the data the hackers took was business data, in the form of software code related to some of its products. The remaining 1% was personal data.
That personal data had been added to the repositories by mistake and should not have been there, as storing it on GitHub went against company policy. Meta has not said what types of personal information were involved.
The company also noted that a significant portion of what looked like personal data was actually synthetic or anonymized test data. As a result, the attackers may not readily be able to tell genuine records apart from test data.
Based on its investigation with GitHub so far, Meta does not believe the hackers were specifically after its data.

More than 20% of the web sits behind Cloudflare’s network, and our team, the Data team, owns the data pipeline responsible for plumbing that data (and more) from our global network to applicable central data centers. The Cloudflare network is a globally distributed system supporting tens of thousands of servers. Data that power Cloudflare Logs, SQL API, observability, internal analytics, and more flow through this network and use our data pipeline to serve customers.
In May of this year, we were providing data delivery at roughly two billion events per second. This includes customer traffic as well as data sent from internal teams. Year after year, we tackle the same problem — exponential traffic growth against linear hardware growth. We have to react to this increase in order to keep resource costs under control. Over the past five years, we’ve made various improvements to compensate for the data volume increase in comparison to hardware allocation, equivalent to deferring two and a half years of hardware expansion. This post details those changes: breaking up our monolithic data schema in 2022, adjusting compression in 2024, rearchitecting pipeline replication in spring 2026, decentralizing sampling in summer 2026, and introducing aggregations into the pipeline in fall 2026.

Artificial Intelligence
Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, which offers a choice of foundation models (FMs) from multiple providers. According to SpaceXAI, Grok 4.7 is trained to work longer on more difficult tasks and knows when to check its own work. That matters most for agents, which carry a task through many steps and must verify what they find along the way.
An agent that works this way has to do more than look things up. It has to form a candidate answer, check it against what it has learned, and refine it until it fits. Grok 4.7 exposes a reasoning effort setting that controls how much deliberation happens before each response, and for agent workloads a practical question is which level to run.
In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three tasks that require search rather than lookup. The tasks are diagnosing a two-service outage from its alerts, scheduling maintenance under interacting constraints, and choosing an optimal set of migrations under a budget. Each task has exactly one correct answer, verified by brute force. We ran all three at every reasoning effort level, six times each, for 72 agent runs.

articles.title: Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images
articles.summary:
Docker has disclosed a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-105445) in Docker Hub that let attackers access another user’s container repositories using a personal access token (PAT).
Docker Hub is an online registry for storing, sharing, and downloading container images - templates that package everything needed for an application to run in an isolated environment.
In Docker Hub, a PAT serves as a secret used to authenticate tools and workflows. It allows you to pull, push, or delete container images.
According to a security bulletin from the Docker team, an attacker could create an account and PAT, then convert the account into an organization and name a target user as its owner.
The CVE-2026-105445 flaw stems from Docker Hub reassigning a personal access token (PAT) to a designated organization owner without changing its secret or obtaining the target's consent. This allowed the attacker to use the token to authenticate as the target.
Depending on the token’s scope and the target’s permissions, attackers could pull, push, or delete images in the target’s repositories and accessible organizations.
“Within the scope of the token, a re-assigned PAT acted as the target user at the registry level, meaning an attacker could potentially pull, push, and/or delete images in the target’s repositories and in organizations where the target had access,” Docker explained.

articles.title: What’s old is new: Lightwell discovers novel zero-day vulnerability in core Java framework
articles.summary:
Enterprise IT runs on decades-old foundational code. The prevailing assumption around these mature components is that if code has been sitting untouched in production for ten years without breaking, it must be safe. Libraries like the Eclipse Implementation of Jakarta XML Binding (JAXB) quietly power enterprise applications in the background. Embedded deep into middleware stacks and application servers, they carry heavy workloads without drawing attention.
Advanced AI security tooling doesn’t ignore these deep-stack layers, however. It finds zero-day flaws hidden in structural parsing logic that standard static analysis tools miss entirely. And discovery is only part of the story. Any new vulnerabilities impacting these load-bearing pillars need to be discovered, analyzed, and swiftly addressed by the community. This is exactly what Lightwell did with a novel vulnerability within JAXB, identified as CVE-2026-92877.
Addressing novel flaws across the software lifecycle
When a vulnerability is discovered in a new framework, communities and maintainers respond quickly. The code is fresh, developers are actively tweaking it, and patches roll out quickly. Legacy components face a different reality. Unaddressed flaws in fundamental XML binding logic can compromise every application server, middleware pipeline, and cloud service that relies on it.

Traditional database architecture assumes you have one or two big database clusters per application, usually accompanied by a connection pooling solution. That model fits D1 particularly well. D1 is Cloudflare's managed, serverless database based on SQLite. It allows you to create millions of databases and only pay for what you use.

Europe has no shortage of semiconductor research. The harder problem often begins after the prototype works.
A company may need an advanced packaging process for a specialized product, but only at volumes of tens, hundreds, or thousands of units. Rolf Aschenbrenner, deputy director of the Fraunhofer Institute for Reliability and Microintegration (IZM), sees that gap regularly. “Companies come to us because their volume is too low to get access to advanced packaging,” he told EE Times. “We can help with prototypes, and in some cases we can also do small-volume manufacturing.”
That doesn’t mean Fraunhofer wants to become an outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider. Its role, according to Aschenbrenner, is to adapt packaging processes to customer requirements, demonstrate their viability, and ultimately hand them off to industry. “The goal is that we also transfer our processes,” he said.
The problem is what happens when no industrial manufacturer is ready to take them.
Too small for the OSATs
Aschenbrenner cited fan-out wafer-level packaging as an example. A company developing RF products might require only around 100 wafers per year. For a large packaging provider, that volume barely registers.

articles.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive through Cloudflare
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of the Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests on an origin’s behalf. The design decision that drew most of the attention is a refusal rather than a feature: the Gateway will not decrypt requests that reach it from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare.
Oblivious HTTP, standardized as RFC 9458, splits a request across two parties. The client encrypts the inner HTTP request to the gateway’s public key using HPKE and sends the sealed payload to a relay. The relay sees the client’s IP address but cannot read the request. The gateway decrypts it and forwards plain HTTP to the application, so it sees the contents but only ever sees the relay’s address.
That only works if different operators run the two hops. Putting a Worker in front of the Gateway, or proxying the relay through Cloudflare, would route the client-identifying hop and the decryption hop through the same company, so Cloudflare built a product that declines to run in that configuration. Authors Lara Schull and Akshat Mahajan write that the model "requires that the relay and app server be operated by separate, non-colluding parties."
For a team evaluating this, the practical cost is the relay. Cloudflare does not supply one for the Gateway, and says the component is not the hard part, since relays "can run on any infrastructure provider, and they’re simple." The hard part is being in a position to "verifiably promise to…

Vulnerabilities in Chrome’s browser, GPU and network processes can now earn researchers up to $20,000. In the case of the renderer process, bug bounty hunters can receive up to $8,000 for use-after-free and memory write bugs.
V8 sandbox vulnerabilities are moving to a flat rate of $5,000, while V8 logic bugs will be rewarded with $4,000.
As for issues not related to memory safety, medium-severity flaws will be rewarded with $2,000 if the vulnerability report includes or directly leads to an identified fix. Sandbox escapes not involving memory safety bugs can get bug bounties of up to $20,000.
Google is also reintroducing a $2,000 fuzzer bonus for developing novel fuzzers.

articles.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
If there’s one lesson the OpenAI-Hugging Face incident taught us, it’s that AI agents can be unpredictable.
“Imagine if something like that happened in the physical world,” Howie Sun, CEO and co-founder of Laplace Intelligence, told TechCrunch. “AI agents are moving from computers into the real world, and we don’t really want physical AI to fail in the real world.”
Ann Arbor-based Laplace is building automated red-teaming — essentially, stress-testing a system by deliberately trying to make it fail — for robotics and physical AI. The company is betting that the only way to make sure physical AI is safe is to have AI test it.
“Our goal is to help companies discover and fix problems before deployment — and, over time, build a shared foundation of evidence that customers, insurers, and regulators can trust,” Sun said.
Laplace is one of 20 startups competing in Startup Battlefield 200, the startup pitch competition taking place at TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco this week, October 13-15. It will present on the Disrupt Stage Tuesday afternoon, October 13.
Sun, alongside his co-founder and chief scientist Henry Liu, founded Laplace a year ago out of the University of Michigan. Sun has spent the last eight years in academia researching how to challenge autonomous driving AI in simulation. In 2023, he and Liu — his then-PhD adviser — published a paper on the subject that made it onto the cover of the top scientific journal Nature. That’s when the calls started coming in from auto…

articles.title: Mitel WX bets next phase of unified communications will be won on the floor, not in the meeting room - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Mitel WX bets next phase of unified communications will be won on the floor, not in the meeting room
For the better part of my 30-year career as an analyst, unified communications has been designed around the person at a desk, bouncing between meetings, chat and email. That made sense when the pandemic pushed everyone onto video.
It makes far less sense when roughly 80% of the global workforce doesn’t sit at a desk at all. In fact, I’ve argued that front-line, non-deskbound workers have been forgotten by most of the UC industry, which is why so many nurses, warehouse workers and others rely on consumer devices and tools.
That’s the gap Mitel Networks Corp. is targeting with Mitel Workforce Experience, which the company recently launched. Mitel WX brings voice, messaging, meetings, contact center and vertical applications into a single client that adapts to the worker’s role rather than the device. Following a pre-briefing I attended with Eric Hanson, Mitel’s executive vice president and chief marketing officer, and Martin Bitzinger, executive vice president of product management, it’s apparent that “toggle tax” across disjointed applications has plagued users for years, so Mitel’s direction addresses a real problem.
Legacy UC is built for everyone, but optimized for no one
Hanson opened with a line that captures the problem with most UC platforms today.

articles.title: Nintendo stands by physical games as Sony embraces a digital-only future — 'There's no plans to ditch physical. We know how much the fans like it as well, so our position has been to be agnostic,' says a Nintendo exec
articles.summary:
Nintendo stands by physical games as Sony embraces a digital-only future — 'There's no plans to ditch physical. We know how much the fans like it as well, so our position has been to be agnostic,' says a Nintendo exec
While Sony remains committed to phasing out physical media, Nintendo is taking the opposite approach. In a recent interview with the Brazilian YouTube channel Coelho no Japão, Bill van Zyll, Nintendo's VP and General Manager for Latin America, confirmed that the company has no plans to abandon cartridges.
"Historically, we’ve been very agnostic, right?" stated van Zyll in the interview.
The Nintendo executive firmly continued, "We go off what the consumer prefers, and take that into account very heavily. We also have a platform that was just launched. We're barely just over a year into NS2. It's got both digital and physical – that capability. There's no plans to ditch physical. We know how much the fans like it as well, so our position has been to be agnostic."
In an era where the gaming industry is rapidly shifting toward digital distribution, it is comforting to see at least some companies still supporting physical media. The core issue with digital purchases is that you do not truly own what you buy; instead, you are purchasing a license to access the game, unlike owning a cartridge or game disc. Some storefronts, such as GOG or itch.io, offer DRM-free downloads of the titles you purchase, but only a handful of them exist.

Microsoft has witnessed skateboarding being modded into Call of Duty and Halo being played in a web browser, and the company is now officially embracing the chaos of this new AI-powered era of game modding.
Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
Microsoft has created a new Xbox Labs group to experiment with decompiling and recompiling games.
Microsoft is putting together a new Xbox Labs group to explore the rapid emergence of these mods, many of which use AI models to help modders remix games in ways we’ve rarely seen before. Xbox Labs will be a “small group of game makers, engineers and scientists whose job is to turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience,” says Xbox CEO Asha Sharma. “We’ll build in the open, learn from what people do, and measure success by whether more people are playing and creating.”
Sharma thinks the experiments we’ve seen in recent weeks, where Windows PC builds have been translated to run on Apple Silicon or ported to run inside browsers, “challenge long-held assumptions about our industry: the tether between software and hardware, the boundary between creation and play, and how people discover and experience games.”

articles.title: Dominion Dynamics strikes deal to build Ukrainian uncrewed ground vehicles in Canada | BetaKit
articles.summary:
Dominion Dynamics has struck a partnership that will send uncrewed ground vehicles from Canada to Ukraine’s front lines.
The news: The Ottawa-based defence contractor signed a memorandum of understanding with Ukrainian defence tech firm Tencore at the Association of the United States Army defence conference in Washington, DC, on Tuesday afternoon. The agreement will see Dominion Dynamics manufacture Tencore’s TerMIT uncrewed ground vehicle in Canada and integrate its AuraNet command-and-control platform to Ukraine’s front lines.
The TerMIT is a modular light armour vehicle that can be modified for logistics, evacuation, or weaponry, and operate without a human on board. Tencore claims it has delivered more than 5,000 uncrewed ground vehicles to Ukrainian military units since 2024.
From the source: “Battlefield requirements change in weeks, so production, operational feedback, and engineering have to run as a loop: build, deploy, learn, change, scale,” Tencore co-founder Roman Tkachenko said in a statement. “Canada gives us the manufacturing base, suppliers and reliable power to run that loop alongside allies who need these vehicles.”
The context: Since launching in June 2025, Dominion Dynamics has raised $169 million CAD to become an explicitly Canadian competitor to big-name defence contractors like Lockheed Martin. Earlier this year, it raised a $139-million CAD Series A round and moved into a 25,000-square-foot manufacturing facility in Ottawa’s west end.

articles.title: Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Rockets are, infamously, a real pain in the butt. Our old friend physics forces rockets to be built with almost no room for error, and even then only a small fraction of their weight makes it to orbit.
There are, at least in theory, other ways to do the job — space elevators, centrifuges, or a big chain hanging from a satellite in space and scooping up cargo from Earth. (Blue Origin spent some time thinking about that one before the idea wound up in a Neal Stephenson novel.)
And then there’s an idea dating all the way back to Jules Verne: Use a big gun to shoot a projectile into space.
Longshot Space Technology, a startup based in Alameda, California, is working on exactly that. The co-founders, CEO Mike Grace and CTO Nato Saichek, see an opportunity to take a technology that has already proven its worth and apply it to the pressing need for space launch. The startup has raised about $20 million from venture investors in service of its mission.
When it comes to frontier technology, Grace says, “you can build something that has a lot of novelty, or you can do something really hard. You don’t get to do both.” He points to SpaceX as an example of a company that has “taken classically de-risked technology and scaled it aggressively.” What SpaceX did with NASA rocket research, he says, Longshot will do with multi-injection guns — designs that give a projectile extra boosts as it moves down the barrel — built for World War II and during 1960s research programs.

AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
- Date:
- October 13, 2026
- Source:
- Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München
- Summary:
- A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.
- Share:
Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

Artificial Intelligence

Security analysts need fast answers about their cloud infrastructure without deep familiarity with domain-specific query languages. Orca Security’s tool covers over 900 cloud models (the resource types Sonar tracks, such as an Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance or an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket). Querying that data required precise model names, nested relationship navigation, and selection from 18 operators (comparison functions like equals or contains used to filter results).
To solve this, Orca Security partnered with AWS to build Discovery AI, a natural language query agent on Amazon Bedrock. Orca provides context-aware security for cloud, code, and AI, and Sonar is its domain-specific query system where users search, filter, and explore across the entire data graph.
In this post, we share the architecture and results of Discovery AI, which converts a natural language question into a Sonar query. As a result, Orca reduced query costs by 90 percent, input tokens by 93 percent, and latency by 75 percent compared to the initial baseline.

articles.title: AWS Reworks EventBridge Custom Buses for Enterprise-Scale Event-Driven Architectures
articles.summary:
AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented. The new model allows organisations to create a single event bus shared across multiple AWS accounts, while adding native event ordering, retention and replay, content-based deduplication, simplified subscriptions and a new pricing model.
The change addresses an architectural tension in enterprise AWS environments. Organisations commonly use multiple accounts to provide isolation between teams and applications, but this can lead to EventBridge buses being connected through cross-account rules and forwarding configurations. As the number of consumers grows, the resulting topology becomes harder to govern and understand, while forwarding the same event through multiple buses can introduce additional processing and routing costs. AWS's new model instead positions a central bus as an organisational event backbone, with individual teams managing their own subscriptions.
The enhanced Custom Event Bus can be shared across AWS accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). A platform team can therefore establish a central event bus while allowing application teams to publish and subscribe from their own accounts. AWS says the new bus supports up to 10,000 subscribers by default, with the option to request a higher quota.

XMEMS starts mass-producing chips that cool AI glasses, smartphones and data centers
Silicon chip startup xMEMS Labs Inc. today said it has started mass production of its XMC-2400 and XMC-4800 chips for cooling artificial intelligence hardware.
No one has commercialized solid-state active cooling at this scale before, according to the company.
The chips are aimed at AI hardware running into heat limits in two places. Conventional fans “simply cannot fit” in AI glasses and smartphones that still need active heat removal, said Mike Housholder, vice president and general manager of the thermal management business unit at xMEMS. For data centers, the company is targeting solid-state drives, laser modules and other parts left outside the liquid cooling that increasingly surrounds high-power processors.
The technology behind both chips came out of the company’s speaker business, where an electrical signal flexes a thin silicon membrane to produce sound. In the cooling chips, the same type of membrane moves air. Device makers can route the air down narrow channels to a processor or a memory chip, the company said, since it builds high pressure.
Nothing in the package spins. Because each device is a single piece of silicon, Housholder said, it could eventually be packaged together with the AI processors it cools.

También ha sido una gran noticia, porque aporta información muy útil sobre la galaxia de la que proviene y, de paso, da respuestas a uno de los muchos misterios del Universo.
Más lejos que nunca. La FRB en cuestión se llama FRB 20240304B y fue detectada en primer lugar por el radiotelescopio MeerKAT, ubicado en Sudáfrica. Supera notablemente el anterior récord, ya que la ráfaga procedía de 8.000 años luz de distancia.
Fósiles cósmicos. Las FRB son destellos de ondas de radio muy intensos, que ocurren solo una vez, en un periodo cortísimo de tiempo. En apenas unos pocos milisegundos, liberan más energía que la que genera el Sol en todo un año. articles.title: Agentic AI Automates RTL Waveform Analysis And Debugging (Columbia, Google)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Columbia University, Google DeepMind, and Google published a technical paper titled “Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification.”
Abstract
“The unprecedented computational scale of modern artificial intelligence depends on complex, multi-billion-transistor Systems-on-Chip, yet the workflows that verify these chips remain stubbornly manual. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have made rapid inroads into Electronic Design Automation (EDA), approximately 74.6% of existing studies target static Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code generation, leaving post-simulation verification and interactive waveform debugging largely untouched. We introduce Back-to-the-Future (BTTF), an end-to-end agentic framework that closes this infrastructural gap. BTTF distills massive, unstructured simulation dumps into a normalized relational SQLite database and couples it with a collaborative multi-agent orchestration engine that translates natural-language verification queries into schema-aware SQL while correlating signal anomalies with versioned RTL repositories. Across a 150-query benchmark, BTTF attains 95.33% execution accuracy, charting a practical path toward autonomous EDA verification.”
Find the technical paper here. October 2026.

AI agents increasingly need to access web resources that are priced per request. For example, premium datasets charge by the query, research APIs meter by the call, and paywalled publishers gate content behind payment. When an AI agent encounters one of these resources, the server returns HTTP 402 Payment Required. The agent has no built-in payment mechanism, no budget attached to the session, and no programmatic way to satisfy the request. The task stalls and requires manual intervention.
Anchor Browser with Agentic Payments handles machine-to-machine payment workflows on behalf of the agent. Developed in collaboration with the AWS Generative AI Innovation Center Partner Agent Factory, it’s now available on AWS Marketplace. This post covers how Anchor Browser integrates with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore payments so that AI agents can pay for x402-protected pages and APIs autonomously. The x402 protocol is an open standard for HTTP-based machine-to-machine payments. A server responds with 402 Payment Required along with the amount, accepted payment methods, and payment address that the agent uses to complete the transaction.

articles.title: High-speed video reveals how honey bee stingers pump venom
articles.summary:
Honey bees are known to leave their stingers embedded in tender flesh once they sting you and fly away. Scientists have now determined that the stinger is able to continue pumping venom into its unfortunate victim even after the bee flies away, thanks to a unique double-piston pump-like mechanism, according to a new paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Different species have evolved different mechanisms for delivering venom, which involves piercing the skin and then pumping venom from a gland or reservoir. Spiders, for instance, have muscles surrounding their venom glands, which contract and eject venom through hollow fangs. Bees, wasps, and ants deliver venom via their stingers, either by contracting muscles around the venom reservoir or through stiff elements called lancets working together to pump venom.
Honey bees (Apis mellifera) add a unique feature: Worker bees fly away after inserting their stingers in the target, leaving the stinger behind. The stinger continues to penetrate the tissue and pump venom on its own, a rare phenomenon known as autotomy. A honey bee’s stinger has three main interlocking elements that form the venom canal: a stylet that widens to form the main pumping chamber and two sharp-tipped lancets that slide back and forth, piercing the tissue and pumping venom into the target. But the precise mechanism by which the pumping action is achieved has never been directly observed.

articles.title: Adenocarcinoma de pulmão: o que é a doença detectada no Papa Leão XIV
articles.summary:
O Papa Leão XIV passou por uma cirurgia na terça-feira (13) para retirar um nódulo do pulmão direito. Os médicos detectaram um adenocarcinoma pulmonar, o tipo mais comum de câncer de pulmão.
O tumor costuma crescer mais lentamente do que outras formas da doença e se desenvolve na região periférica dos pulmões. Quando identificado precocemente, há mais chances de tratamento antes que se espalhe para outros órgãos.
O que é o adenocarcinoma de pulmão
O adenocarcinoma surge nas células glandulares que produzem muco e, na maioria dos casos, se forma nos alvéolos, estruturas responsáveis pelas trocas gasosas nos pulmões. Ele faz parte do grupo dos cânceres de pulmão de não pequenas células (CPNPC).
Em comparação com outros tumores desse grupo, tem maior probabilidade de ser detectado antes de atingir outros órgãos. Embora o tabagismo seja a principal causa do câncer de pulmão, o adenocarcinoma também afeta pessoas que nunca fumaram e é mais frequente entre mulheres e jovens.
Fatores de risco e sintomas
Além do cigarro, a exposição ao fumo passivo, ao radônio, aos gases de escapamento de motores a diesel e a substâncias como amianto, alcatrão, níquel, cromo e berílio pode aumentar o risco de desenvolver a doença.
O adenocarcinoma pode evoluir sem sinais claros no início. Quando aparecem, os sintomas podem ser confundidos com os de outros problemas de saúde. Entre as manifestações possíveis estão:

Workday is opening up its platform and allowing developers to build their own HR and finance agents in Claude Code, Cursor, and other tools, as long as those agents follow the same rules as the people using them.

The X-Files, la icónica serie de FOX, prepara su regreso con una nueva versión de la mano de Ryan Coogler. Hulu ha dado el visto bueno a una nueva producción creada por el director de Black Panther y Sinners, que funcionará como una suerte de reboot del título original.
La nueva serie de The X-Files no tendrá a David Duchovny y Gillian Anderson como protagonistas, pero tampoco pondrá a nuevos actores en la piel de los icónicos Fox Mulder y Dana Scully. Esto significa que el proyecto presentará a dos nuevos personajes originales interpretados por Himesh Patel y Danielle Deadwyler.
De acuerdo con la sinopsis oficial de la nueva serie de The X-Files, Patel y Deadwyler darán vida a dos agentes del FBI muy diferentes, pero con una química muy especial, que son asignados a una división que lleva mucho tiempo cerrada y que se encarga de casos relacionados con fenómenos no explicados.
A primera vista, es lógico pensar que la serie de Ryan Coogler intentará replicar la dinámica original de Mulder y Scully. Sin embargo, no está claro si la nueva serie de The X-Files será un reboot total o si tomará algunos elementos del título original y lo reimaginará para un público más actual. Tampoco se sabe si Duchovny y Anderson pueden llegar a tener alguna participación invitada o si se busca hacer borrón y cuenta nueva a nivel argumental.
The X-Files tendrá nueva serie en Hulu

articles.title: Fairphone’s latest repairable earbuds are smaller, lighter, and longer-lasting
articles.summary:
Repairable, ethical phone brand Fairphone has released its second pair of earbuds. The Fairbuds 2 are just as repairable as the first generation, but deliver improved audio and almost twice the battery life. The Fairbuds 2 are out now in the UK and Europe from £99 / €119, and a US launch at $119 will follow on November 2nd.
Fairphone’s latest repairable earbuds are smaller, lighter, and longer-lasting
The Fairbuds 2 are just as repairable as the first pair, and are launching in the US.
The Fairbuds 2 have been redesigned from the ground up, moving to a stemmed design, available in black or green, and a case that’s 37 percent smaller than the first generation. Despite that shrinking hardware, Fairphone has almost doubled the buds’ battery life, which now totals 40 hours without active noise cancellation, with eight hours on the buds alone, dropping to six with ANC on. Charging is over USB-C, and takes a couple hours for a full top-up. Sadly Qi wireless charging isn’t supported — though it isn’t on Apple’s $129 AirPods 5 either.
I never used the original Fairbuds, but sound should be improved here thanks to new bio-cellulose dynamic drivers, though still at the same 11mm size, plus refined ANC and new support for the LDAC codec. Multipoint connectivity supports two devices at once, and a five-band EQ in the app lets you fine-tune audio.

articles.title: Niobia takes the guesswork out of some of tech's most expensive mistakes | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
San Francisco-based startup Niobia is betting big on a critical but often overlooked part of battery and chip making: helping engineers understand how and why things go wrong. Its AI software flags production defects and lets engineers ask a chatbot what caused them, aiming to deliver answers in minutes rather than days.
How it works (broadly): The company’s customers place AI agents on their production lines to look for defects, then loop in human engineers to work out what might cause a product to fail. The agents run on self-contained GPUs mounted directly on manufacturing equipment, much like a sensor. They can spot pinhole-sized flaws such as scratches. Niobia’s AI also gathers all the data in one place so engineers can ask a chatbot what went wrong and dig deeper into the cause.
Speed is so critical because chips and batteries are some of the world’s most important products, while also increasingly in short supply. As manufacturers continue to develop and improve their technologies, things inevitably go awry during research and development. Engineers then spend days or longer figuring out a fix before they can restart production. Each flaw or mistake can prove costly — sometimes running into the millions of dollars — and set back manufacturing timelines.
Niobia co-founders Gaurav Jha and Harveen Kaur both have PhDs in chemistry and have worked at chipmakers and battery manufacturers, giving them firsthand experience with the challenges within the industry. In a call ahe…

IA tem menos regras que uma caixa de leite, diz Microsoft
Presidente Brad Smith compara IAs a produtos cotidianos, enquanto CEO Satya Nadella defende um “freio de emergência” para interromper modelos.
As inteligências artificiais estão sujeitas a menos exigências de segurança do que produtos cotidianos, como máquinas de lavar e caixas de leite. É o que afirma o presidente da Microsoft, Brad Smith, que defendeu regras mais rígidas e a criação de normas de monitoramento e responsabilização das empresas por acidentes.
Em entrevista à BBC, Smith disse que “toda caixa de leite que você vê na mercearia passa por regras de segurança e inspeção” e que, por isso, “sabemos que ele é seguro”. Para ele, é esse tipo de confiança que a indústria precisa gerar para a IA.
Entre as medidas que possibilitariam isso estão notificações de pessoas afetadas por incidentes e avaliações independentes de sistemas avançados antes da liberação pública. A defesa de regras mais rígidas também se soma à posição do CEO da Microsoft, Satya Nadella, favorável à criação de mecanismos para pausar ou desligar modelos de IA que apresentem comportamentos inesperados.
Em uma publicação no X, Nadella afirmou que as empresas precisam considerar a possibilidade de seus sistemas serem comprometidos e garantir que pessoas autorizadas possam interromper suas operações. “Devemos presumir que um modelo está comprometido e contê-lo desde o início”, escreveu o CEO.

Security, meanwhile, was something Cisco sold as a separate product line rather than something that was inherent to its infrastructure. Under Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel, Cisco has moved away from that model and embraced openness. That’s why I found Cisco’s announcements at this week’s Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose more interesting for what they reveal about the company than for the products themselves.
As Mike Wheatley outlined in his SiliconANGLE post, Cisco rolled out a new pluggable optics form factor with Nvidia Corp., shipped its first Silicon One G300 systems, introduced the G302 top-of-rack chip and a new out-of-band management platform, and brought its Live Protect runtime security capability to SONiC. His post detailed the announcements, but it’s worth a deeper look at why these matter for artificial intelligence and what they say about a Cisco trying to be both open and secure, neither of which were strengths before Patel.

articles.title: The traditional PC layout might not be the best: unusual GPU placement cuts temperatures by 17°C
articles.summary:
In a nutshell: PC builders have long tried to find the most optimal cooling setups for their components, moving around fans, cables, etc. to find the best configurations. A YouTube channel decided to try something a little different: moving the components themselves. This included shifting the GPU next to a case's side-intake, which resulted in a 17-degree drop in temperatures.
The experiment was carried out by TrashBench, which used an Asus ROG Strix RTX 3080 inside a dual-chamber case. The cooling came from three side-intake fans, a rear exhaust, and a top-mounted 360mm CPU AIO.
The idea was to change component placement without moving the case fans. PCIe riser cables were used so the graphics card could be moved away from its usual slot on the motherboard.
Testing involved looping 3DMark Time Spy alongside 7-Zip running on 12 CPU threads. All fans stayed at fixed RPMs, with each configuration tested for ten minutes and temperatures averaged over the final five.
The GPU's first position was on the case floor, which required the removal of the bottom mesh because it touched the card's fans. GPU temperatures barely changed, but the CPU and motherboard VRM dropped around 4°C and 7°C, respectively. Conventional vertical mounting slightly worsened GPU temperatures while modestly improving everything else.
However, placing the card directly against the side intake made all the difference. GPU core temperatures fell 16.7°C, the hotspot dropped 19.3°C, and VRAM cooled by 14°C. Moth…

articles.title: The unfinished business of a startup's collapse
articles.summary:
First published on October 11, 2026
Image Source: TechCabal
Koko Networks raised more than $100 million from international investors to sell subsidised clean cooking stoves, relying on carbon credit sales to help cover their costs. Copia Global raised $123 million to bring e-commerce to smaller towns. Both businesses built sizeable operations around costly problems in African markets. When they collapsed, the question became how much money was left to repay those who had financed their growth.
In February 2026, the administrators of Copia estimated the realisable value of its assets at KES 206.6 million ($1.6 million), while its liabilities were considerably greater than that figure. Similarly, Koko Networks (UK) Limited had accumulated significant debt as a result of regulatory and commercial problems that had disrupted its carbon credit business.
The two failures expose a less visible side of venture capital. Raising millions and reaching customers does not guarantee that a business will have enough cash or saleable assets to meet its obligations. When the money runs out, investors are not the only ones who lose. Suppliers, employees and lenders must pursue claims against what remains, often through lengthy court proceedings that determine who gets paid and how much.

articles.title: ZCS Command Injection via SNMP Handlers Enables Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution
articles.summary:
A critical remote command execution vulnerability affecting the Zimbra Collaboration Suite mail platform has come under active, widespread exploitation, allowing adversaries to harvest complete mailbox archives and persistent authentication credentials without prior system access.
The defect, tracked as CVE-2026-73570, carries a CVSS score of 8.9 and stems from improper input sanitisation inside the platform's SNMP notification subsystem. When paired with public-facing mail transfer agents, the pipeline permits unauthenticated remote attackers to inject arbitrary operating system commands that execute under the context of the underlying Zimbra operating system user account.
Maintainer Synacor initially addressed the vulnerability quietly in Zimbra Collaboration Suite version 10.1.20 on July 20, 2026, but delayed public disclosure until August 13, 2026. During this multi-week disclosure lag, adversaries reverse-engineered the binary changes and launched scanning campaigns against public instances. Telemetry captured by Microsoft and Polish national cybersecurity agency CERT Polska confirmed that threat groups actively probed enterprise mail infrastructure throughout late July and August, deploying backdoors before most operations teams recognised the severity of the patch.

articles.title: Un micro caché dans du papier toilette chez OpenAI : un ingénieur saoudien arrêté par le FBI
articles.summary:
Un enregistreur branché sur un port USB derrière un téléviseur et dissimulé dans… du papier toilette. C’est le dispositif découvert le 30 septembre dans une salle de réunion d’OpenAI, à San Francisco, a annoncé la firme sur X. Un endroit où se discutent des informations confidentielles sur les recherches, les futurs produits et la stratégie du créateur de ChatGPT.
L’affaire a été rendue publique le 13 octobre 2026 par les autorités américaines. Quatre jours plus tôt, le FBI avait arrêté Abdulrahman Alfozan, un ingénieur saoudien de 35 ans employé par OpenAI depuis juillet 2025, soupçonné d’avoir installé l’appareil. Sana, which Workday bought for $1.1 billion last year, is available now, and admins can roll it out to their users without making it the default.
Picking components instead of writing them
Joel Hellermark, Workday’s chief AI officer and Sana’s founder, said in a press briefing that the usual approach to generative UI, in which a model generates the full interface, is “quite slow.”
“If you use a classification model instead and you just give it all of the design components to pick from, you can literally do it instantly,” he said.
Workday gave Jev every atomic component in its design system and hard-coded none of the selection logic, Hellermark said, though the team also had to get data preloading right. In the demo, the paycheck card appeared before he finished typing, for example.

According to Microsoft, the latest updates resolve 1,413 CVEs, including 1,102 affecting Windows, 134 in Office, 61 in developer tools, and 36 in SharePoint Server. Exchange Server, Azure, Defender, and other products also received security patches.
This month alone, Microsoft patched more vulnerabilities than it did in all of 2025. The surge, largely driven by AI, has pushed the number of flaws fixed so far in 2026 past 4,000.
The exploited zero-day is tracked as CVE-2026-96951 (CVSS score 8.8/10). Microsoft describes it as a Windows shell security feature bypass flaw that enables an attacker to evade Mark of the Web (MotW) defenses.
MotW tags internet-downloaded files, signaling security mechanisms like Defender SmartScreen and Office Protected View to restrict automatic execution. Bypassing MotW allows malicious files to launch without triggering warnings.
“In an email or instant message attack scenario, the attacker could send the targeted user a specially crafted file that is designed to exploit the vulnerability,” the tech giant explained in its advisory. “In any case an attacker would have no way to force a user to view attacker-controlled content. Instead, an attacker would have to convince a user to take action.”

Publiée le 12 octobre 2026 dans la revue Nature Cities, une étude pilotée par Shengli Tao et Xie Hu, chercheurs à l'université de Pékin, a mesuré entre 2014 et 2023 les mouvements verticaux du sol dans 465 villes de plus d'un million d'habitants, réparties sur 107 pays. Le phénomène porte un nom, la subsidence : un tassement lent qui lézarde les façades, tord les canalisations et aggrave les inondations. Les auteurs revendiquent la première évaluation planétaire menée avec une méthode homogène, là où les travaux antérieurs juxtaposaient des études locales aux protocoles disparates.

In February 2007, the hulking dual-rotor casualty evacuation helicopter had just flown three wounded soldiers to a field hospital in Balad, north of Baghdad, when another call came: an emergency mission to fly through an insurgent-controlled area in broad daylight. Typically, helicopters would be in a spot like this only at night, and with all lights turned off.
As it passed near the city of Karmah, in the eastern side of Al-Anbar province, an insurgent fired a portable missile launcher. The tail gunner, who likely saw the shot roaring in, yelled for the pilot to make an evasive move. But the missile had already locked on, and the ensuing blast started a fire on board. After the pilot battled the failing machine for 58 agonizing seconds, Morphine 1-2 plunged to the ground. All seven crew members were killed.

articles.title: Licube wants to be the fuel provider to the fusion power industry — see how at TechCrunch Disrupt | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
If fusion power pans out, and there are signs that it will, the world will need a lot more lithium.
That’s the bet behind Licube, a startup that has licensed technology from Hirosaki University in Japan, to purify lithium-6, the form of lithium that fusion plants need to make their own fuel, out of naturally occurring lithium.
The reason comes down to the fuel supply. A lot of things have to go right for fusion power to hit the grid, and one of them is the fuel. Most planned plants would run on a mix of two fuels, deuterium and tritium. Deuterium is easy to come by, but tritium is extremely rare in nature, and it’s an open secret in the fusion world that there isn’t enough of it to power every planned plant.
The proposed workaround is to make tritium on site, inside the power plant itself. A fusion reaction gives off a stream of fast-moving particles called neutrons. Startups plan to surround the reactor with a blanket of lithium, so that when a neutron strikes a lithium atom, the atom splits into helium and tritium. The tritium can then be collected, purified, and fed back into the reactor as fuel.
Not all lithium does this job equally well. It comes in two slightly different forms, lithium-6 and lithium-7, named for their weights. Lithium-6 is far better at capturing neutrons and producing tritium, but it makes up only about 7.5% of natural lithium, and the rest is the heavier lithium-7. Separating the two is difficult, and there is little capacity to do it today, so the wo…

Qilimanjaro Quantum Tech, Spain’s only full-stack quantum computing company, has announced the first close of its Series A funding round at €19.6 million.
The round was led by Indra Group through IndraMind, its sovereign artificial intelligence initiative, with a €10 million investment. The Spanish Society for Technological Transformation (SETT), a public entity under Spain’s Ministry for Digital Transformation and Public Administration, also renewed its backing with a further €9.6 million investment.
“Quantum computing will mark a decisive leap in the evolution of artificial intelligence and its ability to solve highly complex problems. With this transaction, Indra Group strengthens its position in this strategic field, while IndraMind expands the capabilities it can use to develop sovereign, differentiated solutions for defence, security and industry,” said Ignacio Martínez, General Manager of IndraMind.
Qilimanjaro Quantum Tech was founded in Barcelona in 2019 as a spin-off of IFAE, BSC and the University of Barcelona by Dr. Pol Forn Díaz, Dr. Victor Canivell, Dr. José Ignacio Latorre, Jordi Blasco, and Dr. Artur Garcia Sáez. The company builds full-stack quantum computers, meaning it develops its own chips, software and algorithms and integrates cryogenics and control electronics into complete systems.

articles.title: Spranic builds spatial memory for physical AI - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Spranic builds spatial memory for physical AI
Physical AI needs context about its surroundings to adapt beyond a fixed set of instructions.
Munich-based Spranic is building a spatial memory layer that records physical spaces and how they change. Connecting that information with knowledge graphs could help robots interpret their environments across different tasks, according to Jordi Spranger (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of Spranic.
“Robots deserve the right context at the right time across domains,” he said. “This is the problem we’re tackling. We can see that this works really well for digital agents already. Now we’re bringing this to the physical world.”
Spranger spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier for theCUBE + NYSE Wired: AI Luminaries interview series on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how knowledge graphs could help robots adapt tasks and make their decisions auditable. (* Disclosure below.)
Giving physical AI reusable context
Adapting machines to changing environments remains a challenge for physical AI. Reusable spatial context can reduce the task-specific planning required for robot deployments, according to Spranger.
“But for robots, maps are a really big part,” he said. [Robots] need Google Maps on steroids to be really free from a statically planned task [so they] can replan across a lot of tasks that a humanoid could do.”
Flexibility also requires knowing where a robot’s information comes from, accordi…

articles.title: Google wants to host your personal vibe-coded apps in the Play Store
articles.summary:
Google has already added a few AI features to the Play Store, but a lot more are coming. The previously released Ask Play feature is expanding to offer more AI-powered discovery options in Google’s app store, and Google is also using AI to build a recommendation engine called Game Finder. For people who have embraced AI to build their own apps, the Play Store will soon offer a way to privately host and share those creations.
Google rolled out Ask Play in 2025 as a small chatbot interface on Play Store listings. It lets you ask questions about an app or game, either by typing it in manually or choosing from a list of suggested queries. Starting today, Ask Play is expanding into a more general way to search for apps and games. You ask the robot questions, and it generates recommendations that can include detailed comparison charts. Gemini will roll out a similar capability soon.
Google’s other AI discovery announcement focuses on games. The new Game Finder feature leans on all the usage data Google’s app platform has hoovered up over the years, featuring insights into the way 1.2 billion people play games on Android. It builds a profile called Gamer DNA and matches you with players who have similar DNA.
You can tune your DNA profile by rating the games you’ve played, which supposedly leads to more accurate recommendations. There will be game playlists to peruse, along with various contextual lists like relaxing, trending titles, and more specific lists based on mechanics you’ve…

articles.title: Meta lança o Muse Wonder, sua IA mais avançada até agora • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Meta lança o Muse Wonder, sua IA mais avançada até agora
Novos modelos focam em agentes capazes de lembrar informações, usar computadores e executar tarefas.
A Meta apresentou o Muse Wonder e o Muse Wonder Full, seus novos modelos de inteligência artificial voltados para agentes pessoais e profissionais. Segundo a companhia, os sistemas são os mais poderosos que já criou e reforçam a disputa com modelos de ponta das rivais OpenAI e Anthropic.
Os modelos foram treinados para executar tarefas que demandam várias etapas, como analisar contratos, desenvolver aplicativos e utilizar navegadores ou outros programas.
Uma das principais novidades é o recurso Active Memory, que permite ao modelo guardar informações importantes entre diferentes conversas e recuperá-las em novas tarefas. Já o Active Focus foi desenvolvido para manter o agente trabalhando mesmo diante de dificuldades.
Segundo a Meta, o modelo pode tentar métodos alternativos ao encontrar obstáculos, adaptar o plano conforme surgem novas informações e pedir ajuda ao usuário quando necessário. Antes de executar ações consideradas importantes, ele também pede confirmação.
A novidade combina essas funções com capacidade de operar computadores. Em demonstrações, a Meta mostra o Muse Wonder usando um navegador e outros aplicativos para criar e encomendar produtos a partir de fotos de um perfil no Instagram. O modelo também foi treinado para programação e pode dividir um projeto entre subagentes, realizar alterações em vários ar…

articles.title: Flock faces lawsuit after deputies allegedly used its cameras to retaliate against man who sued sheriff
articles.summary:
WTF?! It's not like Flock and its dystopian spying system need any more bad publicity, but here we go: the company and officials from a sheriff's office that uses its cameras are facing a lawsuit from a man who says deputies ran his car through Flock's camera network in retaliation for him suing the sheriff over a previous arrest.
Tyler Murkerson has named Flock, Coweta County, Sheriff Lenn Wood, two sheriff's office employees, and three unidentified operators in his lawsuit. It also seeks class-action status, representing people whose vehicles were searched by Georgia law enforcement without documented investigative justification.
Murkerson previously sued the sheriff and two deputies in Coweta County, alleging that they violated his constitutional rights by forcing him to the ground, using a Taser on him, and arresting him in a gas station parking lot over an alleged seatbelt violation. The suit claims that this happened despite Georgia's seatbelt statute not applying on private property. The criminal charges against him were dismissed in June 2023, and his civil rights lawsuit was resolved in 2026.
While the suit was pending, it's alleged that Coweta County deputies used Flock's ALPR network and associated state and federal law enforcement databases to surveil Murkerson.

articles.title: The agent did the work. The audit log couldn’t say who asked.
articles.summary:
The agent did the work. The audit log couldn’t say who asked.
More than 20 percent of the MCP-related access policies that Shawn Petty’s team reviewed across customer and prospect environments were broken or missing, according to a recent account published in The New Stack. In most cases, the MCP server ran on someone’s personal token rather than a service account.
At 12 p.m. Eastern/9 a.m. Pacific on Tuesday, October 27, Petty, Chief Customer Officer at CloudBolt, and Mike Bombard, Director of Global Pre-Sales Engineering at CloudBolt, will join The New Stack host Viktor Farcic for a live demo of how to trace an agent’s actions back to the person responsible for them.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The problem, though, usually shows up after an incident: That personal token puts an engineer’s name into the audit trail for everything the agent did. Meanwhile, a shared service account puts the account’s name there instead. In both cases, the audit trail isn’t able to identify who precisely asked the agent to do the work or who approved the access it used.
Access that goes through a request, approval, and grant in the identity provider is provisioned, and the identity provider records it. Access that an agent picks up along the way is emergent: A role inherited from the service that launched it, or a developer’s own token lent out to finish a task. “Rockstar commence toujours par la console” : finalement, GTA 6 ne ferait patienter les joueurs PC que quelques mois
Quatre sources de l'industrie l'affirment : la version PC de GTA 6 sortirait entre janvier et mars 2027, quelques semaines à peine après les consoles. Ce calendrier éclair tombe pile au moment où la PS5 cède sous les jailbreaks et où les émulateurs PC commencent à grignoter ses exclusivités.

GTA 6 sur PC : pourquoi Rockstar presserait le pas

articles.title: Cascador and Sterling launch $200 million fund to derisk startup loans
articles.summary: Cascador, a Nigeria-focused platform for growth-stage founders, and Sterling Bank, a mid-size Nigerian commercial bank, have set up a $200 million fund to help small Nigerian businesses and startups get bank loans by sharing the risk of borrowers defaulting. The partners say the SME Credit Backstop can back up to $1 billion in loans at a time. Rather than directly lending to the businesses, it will guarantee part of the bank’s potential losses if a borrower defaults, making it easier for lenders to extend credit to companies they might otherwise consider risky. The fund will consider businesses nominated by venture capital firms and studios that already back them. It will use AI-powered underwriting to check whether the business is ready to take on debt. If it approves the business, the fund agrees to cover part of the bank’s loss if that loan goes bad. The fund targets a persistent obstacle for most Nigerian startups: access to debt. About one in five Nigerian businesses had a bank loan or line of credit in 2025, compared with 22% across Sub-Saharan Africa and 36% globally, according to World Bank Enterprise Survey data . Banks often consider small businesses and startups as risky and demand collateral that many cannot provide. “By sharing risk with lenders and translating community trust into a bankable signal to lend, the fund can help more businesses access what they need to scale and create jobs,” said Trish Thomas, Cascador’s CEO, in a statement shared with TechCabal. articles.title: Funcionária é demitida após recusar “sentinela” que tira foto a cada 3 minutos • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Funcionária é demitida após recusar “sentinela” que tira foto a cada 3 minutos
Monitoramento com IA previa até 160 fotos por dia durante o trabalho no home office. Caso deu origem a processo judicial nos EUA.
Uma funcionária afirma ter sido demitida após se recusar a aceitar um sistema de monitoramento que tiraria cerca de 160 fotos de seu rosto por dia. O caso virou uma ação judicial em Nova Jersey, nos Estados Unidos. Segundo o processo, Glennis Von Sander-Timinski trabalhava de casa na Sutherland Healthcare Solutions desde 2018.
Em agosto, a companhia informou que adotaria uma ferramenta chamada Sentinel AI, que usaria a webcam do notebook para registrar uma imagem a cada três minutos durante um expediente de oito horas. Segundo o processo, o sistema também utilizaria reconhecimento facial para confirmar se a funcionária estava perto do computador.
De início, ela solicitou uma adaptação por preocupação com a privacidade e com os efeitos do sistema sobre a sua saúde. Seu médico enviou uma recomendação para que as capturas fossem menos frequentes, afirmando que o monitoramento estava aumentando o estresse e agravando sintomas de ansiedade.
A ação alega que a empresa não aceitou reduzir a frequência. A funcionária teria recebido como alternativas aceitar o monitoramento, voltar ao trabalho presencial ou deixar a empresa. A ação estima que o deslocamento consumiria aproximadamente seis horas por dia. Ela acabou demitida em 8 de setembro.
